Jordan / team — thanks for the detail. A few legal clarifications from Redwood's side:

1) Additional Insured: Redwood can provide Additional Insured status on a CG-style endorsement. We typically accept either the ISO CG 20 10 or a carrier-equivalent endorsement that grants Additional Insured status for ongoing operations and completed operations to the extent caused by Redwood's acts or omissions. Proposed language we prefer: "Acme Cloud and its affiliates are added as Additional Insured with respect to liability arising out of the named insured's work performed for Acme Cloud."

2) Waiver of Subrogation: Redwood can accept a waiver of subrogation from its insurers to the extent permitted by law, but we don't provide blanket waivers that would impair our insurers' rights where not related to our performance. If Acme requires a full waiver, please confirm whether that's limited to claims caused by Redwood's negligence.

3) Notice of Cancellation: 30 days' notice is standard; we can request that from our carriers. If your procurement requires endorsement wording showing the notice period on the COI, please confirm.

4) Professional Liability / E&O: We carry a separate E&O policy; we will provide policy limits and numbers where available. For cyber-specific requirements (e.g., express first party limits), please point to the contract section referencing cyber coverage so we can confirm there is alignment.

Action items for Acme: please provide the broker contact (name/email) and confirm whether ISO language is mandatory. For our part, we will:
- Request COI and Additional Insured endorsement from our broker.
- Provide a draft endorsement PDF for your review.
- Flag any insurer-level objections if carrier refuses specific waiver language.

If your team prefers, we can accept a redline to the MSA insurance paragraph with the exact endorsement text Acme needs; that will speed review.

Regards,
Dev Patel
